🦃 It's Turkey Eve — prepare the sweatpants. Today's newsletter, edited by Herb Scribner, is 590 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: Presidential envoy Jared Kushner is urging Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to make good on commitments he made to President Trump to implement a Gaza peace plan, Axios' Barak Ravid scoops.
 
 
1 big thing: Iowa's explosive showdown
 
Debris flies skyward this morning as the Army destroys degraded explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. Photo: Scott Olson/Getty Images

🪖 The Army detonated 68 drums of unstable lead azide at an Iowa plant today after multiple delays, a court challenge and intervention from President Trump, Axios' Avery Lotz and Julianna Bragg write.

  • Federal officials have repeatedly stressed that detonating the volatile material was safer than risking a spontaneous explosion.

💥 Two explosions erupted simultaneously in Middletown, Iowa.

  • Large clouds of smoke shot into the air following the detonation, according to reporters at the scene.

🫡 Trump wrote on Truth Social: "Early reports from Iowa are that the Army's mitigation efforts have far exceeded expectations."

  • Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle wrote on X: "The Army's controlled, mitigated detonation exceeded all expectations and was a HUGE success. The threat ... has been eliminated."
  • Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe (R) says from the neighboring state that the detonation was "well-contained," based on early analysis.

💣 Threat level: The explosion raised concerns about exposing residents to lead, for which there are no established safe levels of exposure.

  • Before the blast, officials said they didn't expect the release of the hazardous compounds.

🚧 The evacuation zone was a 5-mile cone extending southwest of the ammunition plant.

2. 💰 Gravy for GDP
 
Data: Bureau of Economic Analysis. Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios

The U.S. economy grew substantially faster this summer than initially thought, Axios' Courtenay Brown writes.

  • The economy is on remarkably strong footing heading into year-end, though inflation remains stubbornly high.

By the numbers: The economy expanded at a 4.3% annualized rate, up from the 3.4% initially reported.

A MESSAGE FROM ANTHROPIC

How a family business uses Claude to stay true to its roots
 
 

Bama Sea Products started in 1977 with two shrimp boats. Today, the Florida-based company competes in a global market using custom tools the team built with Claude to uphold the quality and safety standards the business has always stood for.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
The 7th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade rolls and floats down Broadway on Nov. 27, 1930. Photo: AP
  1. 🎈 The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in Manhattan is facing the threat of grounded balloons. The National Weather Service declared a "high wind watch" for NYC tomorrow morning. Wind grounded balloons in 1971, but the parade has never been canceled due to weather. Get the latest.
  2. 🏈 The Pittsburgh Steelers are benching iconic QB Aaron Rodgers, despite holding a winning 6-4 record, and plan to start Mason Rudolph against the Denver Broncos in Black Friday's game. This is Rodgers' 22nd season in the NFL, which many expect to be his last. Go deeper.
  3. 🚙 The Pentagon is in talks with GM, Ford and other manufacturers to help produce drones in an effort to use the car industry's assembly lines to boost production, The Wall Street Journal reports (gift link).
  4. 🌕 SpaceX won FCC approval to deploy 1 million satellites to help the company create data centers in space. Read the announcement.
 
 
4. 🎮 1 fun thing: 2026's best video games
 
"The Blood of Dawnwalker." Image: Rebel Wolves via AP

🕹️ "The Blood of Dawnwalker" and "Grand Theft Auto VI" top AP's list of 2026's best video games.

  • The top five also include the tactical game "Star Wars Zero Company," the pixelated throwback "Mina the Hollower" and the survival shooter "Resident Evil Requiem."

📊 Stunning stat: "GTA VI" sold more than 47 million units by the end of its launch weekend, per Sensor Tower.

☁️ Thought bubble from Axios' Herb Scribner: I haven't played "Blood of Dawnwalker," but I've spent a few hours playing "GTA VI."

  • It's full of beautiful scenery, dynamic characters and compelling storylines. You want to be in the game driving around, running errands, completing missions. I can't wait to fly another plane and find one of the nine distinct endings.
